facts.statement: The genus Haplocanthosaurus was originally named by John Bell Hatcher in 1903.
facts.quote: authority: Hatcher, 1903 (conserved name)

facts.statement: The original name Haplocanthus was rejected because it was preoccupied by a fish genus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Haplocanthus Hatcher, 1903 (preoccupied; nomen rejectum)

facts.statement: A second species, Haplocanthosaurus delfsi, was described by McIntosh and Williams in 1988.
facts.quote: subdivision: H. delfsi McIntosh & Williams, 1988

facts.statement: The species H. delfsi was discovered by a college student named Edwin Delfs in Colorado and formally described in 1988.
facts.quote: the referred species H. delfsi was discovered by a young college student named Edwin Delfs in Colorado, United States and described by Jack McIntosh and Michael Williams in 1988

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus lived in North America between 155 and 152 million years ago during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: They lived during the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage), 155 to 152 million years ago in North America

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus was one of the smallest Morrison sauropods, reaching a length of 14.8 meters (49 feet) and a weight of 12.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Haplocanthosaurus was one of the smallest sauropods of the Morrison. While some Morrison sauropods could reach lengths of over 20 meters (or over 66 feet), Haplocanthosaurus was smaller, reaching a total length of 14.8 meters (49 feet) and an estimated weight of 12.8 MT

facts.statement: The dorsoventrally elongate oval outlines of the vertebrae are a characteristic feature shared only with Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: The dorsoventrally elongate oval outlines are characteristic of Haplocanthosaurus with only Camarasaurus also possessing them

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus is distinguished by the absence of cranial centrodiapophyseal laminae in its dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Haplocanthosaurus is distinguished by dorsal vertebra lacking cranial centrodiapophyseal laminae

facts.statement: The genus is also distinguished by elongate intrapostzygapophyseal laminae, dorsal transverse processes reaching the height of neural spines, and an expanded distal end of the scapular blade.
facts.quote: Also, it is distinguished by elongate intrapostzygapophyseal laminae, dorsoventrally directed dorsal transverse processes that approach the height of the neural spines, and the distal end of the scapular blade being dorsally and ventrally expanded

facts.statement: José Bonaparte established the family Haplocanthosauridae in 1999 to classify Haplocanthosaurus separately from other sauropods.
facts.quote: Originally described as a "cetiosaurid", José Bonaparte decided in 1999 that Haplocanthosaurus differed enough from other sauropods to warrant its own family, the Haplocanthosauridae

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic relationships of Haplocanthosaurus remain uncertain among scientists.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic studies have failed to clarify the exact relationships of Haplocanthosaurus with any certainty

facts.statement: Studies have produced conflicting results, placing Haplocanthosaurus as a primitive macronarian, a very primitive diplodocoid related to Diplodocus, or a non-neosauropod eusauropod.
facts.quote: Studies have variously found it to be more primitive than the neosauropods, a primitive macronarian (related to the ancestor of more advanced forms such as Camarasaurus and the brachiosaurids), or a very primitive diplodocoid, more closely related to Diplodocus than to titanosaurs, but more primitive than rebbachisaurids

facts.statement: Four specimens of Haplocanthosaurus are currently known: one of H. delfsi and three of H. priscus.
facts.quote: There are four known specimens of Haplocanthosaurus: one of H. delfsi, and three of H. priscus

facts.statement: The type specimen of H. delfsi is the only known specimen complete enough to be mounted for display.
facts.quote: Of these, the type of H. delfsi is the only one complete enough to mount

facts.statement: The mounted H. delfsi specimen at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History features a speculative replica skull because the actual skull was never found.
facts.quote: The mounted specimen of H. delfsi now stands in the Cleveland Museum of Natural History, albeit with a completely speculative replica skull, as the actual skull was not recovered

facts.statement: Additional specimens from a different region of the Morrison Formation were assigned to Haplocanthosaurus in 2014.
facts.quote: Recently described specimens from a different region of the Morrison Formation were assigned to Haplocanthosaurus in 2014

facts.statement: A controversial potential specimen nicknamed "Big Monty" found in Montana has been claimed to be 110 feet long, but its validity is debated.
facts.quote: One potential specimen has been nicknamed "Big Monty," for its discovery in Montana. It has been claimed to measure an incredible 110 ft long. However, much controversy surrounds the specimen and, as such, little is truly known about it

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur whose name means "simple-spine lizard".
facts.quote: Haplocanthosaurus (gr. "lagarto de espinazo simple") es un género de dinosaurio saurópodo

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 156 to 144 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 156 y 144 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: The name refers to the simple dorsal spines on its vertebrae, which were not double-spined like other sauropods from the same formation.
facts.quote: El nombre hace referencia a las espinas dorsales de las vértebras, al ser simples y no dobles como en otros saurópodos de la misma formación

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus was first discovered by a young college student named Edwin Delfs in Colorado.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto por primera vez por un joven estudiante universitario llamado Edwin Delfs en Colorado

facts.statement: Two incomplete skeletons were discovered in Colorado and described in 1903 as Haplocanthus priscus.
facts.quote: A principios de , se descubrieron dos esqueletos incompletos en Colorado, Estados Unidos, los cuales fueron descritos en 1903 como Haplocanthus priscus

facts.statement: The name was changed from Haplocanthus priscus to Haplocanthosaurus utterbacki and then to H. priscus in 1903 because the original name was occupied by a fish.
facts.quote: Al estar ocupado el nombre por un pez acantodio, se cambió a Haplocanthosaurus utterbacki y luego a H. priscus en 1903

facts.statement: A second species, Haplocanthosaurus delfsi, was named in 1988 from material originally classified by Marsh in 1889 as Morosaurus agilis.
facts.quote: En 1988, una segunda especie fue nombrada a partir de material originalmente clasificado por Marsh en 1889 como Morosaurus agilis, bajo el nombre de Haplocanthus delfsi

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus was one of the smallest sauropods of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Haplocanthosaurus fue uno de los saurópodos más pequeños de Morrison

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus reached a total length of around 15 meters and an estimated weight of 13 tonnes.
facts.quote: alcanzando una longitud total de alrededor de 15 metros y un peso estimado de 13 toneladas

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus had front legs longer than its hind legs, giving its back a downward curve.
facts.quote: Poseían patas delanteras más largas que las traseras lo que le otorgaba a la espalda una curva descendente

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus had a long neck with 14 vertebrae and a whip-like tail.
facts.quote: Presentaban un cuello largo con 14 vértebras y una cola en forma de látigo

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus is known from many elements, primarily vertebrae.
facts.quote: Haplocanthosaurus es conocido por muchos elementos, principalmente de vértebras

facts.statement: There are four known specimens of Haplocanthosaurus: one of H. delfsi and three of H. priscus.
facts.quote: Hay cuatro especímenes conocidos de Haplocanthosaurus, uno de H. delfsi y tres de H. priscus

facts.statement: The mounted specimen is now located in the Cleveland Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: El espécimen montado ahora se encuentra en el Museo de Historia Natural de Cleveland

facts.statement: The mounted specimen has a completely speculative skull replica because the real skull was never recovered.
facts.quote: aunque con una réplica de cráneo completamente especulativa, ya que el cráneo real no fue recuperado

facts.statement: A potential specimen nicknamed "Big Monty" discovered in Montana has been claimed to measure an incredible 33 meters in length.
facts.quote: Un espécimen potencial ha sido apodado "Big Monty" por su descubrimiento en Montana. Se ha afirmado que mide un increíble 33 metros de largo

facts.statement: There is much controversy surrounding the "Big Monty" specimen, and very little is known about it.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, hay mucha controversia alrededor del espécimen y, como tal, se sabe muy poco al respecto

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus is considered the last of the cetiosaurids.
facts.quote: El haplocantosaurio es considerado como el último de los cetiosáuridos

facts.statement: In 1999, José Fernando Bonaparte decided that Haplocanthosaurus differed enough from other sauropods to warrant its own family, Haplocanthosauridae.
facts.quote: José Fernando Bonaparte decidió en 1999 que Haplocanthosaurus difiere los bastante de otros saurópodos para autorizar su propia familia, la Haplocanthosauridae

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies have failed to clarify the exact relationships of Haplocanthosaurus beyond doubt.
facts.quote: Estudios filogenéticos han fallado en clarificar las exactas relaciones de Haplocanthosaurus más halla de toda duda

facts.statement: Studies have found various positions for Haplocanthosaurus, including being the most primitive neosauropod, a primitive macronarian related to the ancestor of Camarasaurus and brachiosaurids, or a very primitive diplodocoid.
facts.quote: Los estudios han encontrado varias posiciones entre ellas el de ser el más primitivos que los neosaurópodos, un macronaria primitivo, relacionado con el ancestro de formas más avanzadas como Camarasaurus y los braquiosáuridos), o un muy primitivo diplodocoide

facts.statement: The parent group of Haplocanthosaurus is Diplodocoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Diplodocoidea

facts.statement: Haplocanthosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The time range for Haplocanthosaurus is from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 11 recorded fossil occurrences of Haplocanthosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 11

rejected.quote: Haplocanthosaurus specimens have been found in the lowermost layer of the Morrison Formation
